The absorber achieves 99% absorptivity at 1.54 μm wavelength
The 1.54 μm resonance peak has a full-width at half-maximum (FWHM) of only 40 nm
The 6.2 μm resonance peak has a FWHM of 1 μm
The absorber reduces scattering of 1.54 μm IR laser light by more than 90%
MWIR and LWIR signatures are suppressed by more than 92%
Signal reduction rates remain greater than 90% across temperatures from room temperature to 500°C
The unit cell period is 1.34 μm
The disk radius is 0.168 μm
The ring outer radius is 600 nm
The ring inner radius is 500 nm
The top silver (Ag) layer thickness is 0.18 μm
The polyimide (PI) insulator layer thickness is 0.1 μm
The ring thickness is 100 nm
At 10° incident angle, the 1.54 μm peak magnitude decreases by 25%
The 1.54 μm resonance wavelength remains fixed with only 40 nm variations at incident angles up to 10°
The 6.2 μm peak maintains nearly constant absorptivity up to 50° incident angle
The absorber has very low emissivity in the LWIR range (8-14 μm)
The relative permittivity of the dielectric (polyimide) is 2.56
The relative permittivity of silver is -85.5
The SPP and MP resonance peaks are simultaneously matched at 1.54 μm to achieve incident angle insensitivity
The disk and ring components are designed to excite MPs independently without interference
The absorber maintains performance across different polarizations due to circular symmetry of unit cells
Wavelength shifts with polarization angle variations are negligible compared to peak bandwidths
The absorber was designed to suppress IR signatures used by both laser-guided missiles and thermal imaging devices
The paper used finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulation and inductor-capacitor circuit model (ICCM) for design and analysis
